title: Topology-aware latency-slice router for multi-region failover
creator: Priya Srinivasan
description: Problem: We currently observe p99 latency spikes and partial outages when a single region loses capacity; existing geo-weighted routing reacts slowly and causes cross-region cascades. Goal: ship a topology-aware router that routes by latency slices, honors geo-pinning for session affinity, and is capacity-aware so it gracefully sheds traffic and triggers circuit breakers before SLOs are violated. Success criteria: 30% reduction in p99 across cross-region failovers, maintain P95 SLO within 1.2x baseline during simulated region failure, automated rollback safe by canary and feature flagging. Non-goals: rewriting the serving runtime; we will integrate with existing runtime hints and autoscaling signals.
design_decisions: Chosen approach: latency-slice routing. We maintain per-region latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) and capacity tokens. Incoming requests are bucketed into latency-sensitive slices (interactive: p95 target 200ms, background: p95 target 2s). For each slice we compute a weighted score: score = latency_penalty * (1 + short_term_load_factor) / capacity_token_fraction. Regions with score above threshold are deprioritized; if all regions exceed safe thresholds we trigger controlled load shedding by rejecting lowest-priority slices or rerouting to pre-configured fallback variants. We opted for a latency-slice model instead of pure threshold eviction to avoid brittle oscillation when absolute thresholds are noisy. Hysteresis windows (60s) and exponential backoff on re-enablement reduce flapping.
tradeoffs: Complexity vs precision: adding per-slice scoring increases routing complexity but yields better tail-latency guarantees. Cost: may increase cross-region egress in some failover scenarios—mitigated by preferring region-local cache hits and honoring geo-pinning TTL where available. Observability: requires richer telemetry (per-region p95/p99 + healthy_capacity estimate) — dependency on telemetry infra.
circuit_breaker_policy: Triggers: (1) sustained error rate > 3% for 3m; (2) p99 > 1.5x slice target for 2m; (3) capacity tokens depleted below 10% of baseline for two consecutive windows. Actions: soft-fail traffic for 5% of requests (reject with 429 and standardized Retry-After), escalate to regional ejection for 30s with exponential backoff. All breakers run per-customer-tier and per-model-tag to avoid noisy neighbor impact.
rollout_plan: 1) Unit + integration tests in routing sim harness. 2) Canary: 2% traffic in us-west1 for 48h with synthetic load (latency profiles) and real traffic shadowing. 3) Gradual ramp to 25% across regions in 3 phases with automated health gates (p95 <= 1.1x baseline AND error rate <= baseline + 0.5%). 4) Full rollout behind feature flag; immediate rollback path via kill-switch route to legacy dispatcher.
telemetry_and_alerts: New Grafana dashboards (latency-slice overview, per-region capacity tokens, circuit-breaker events). Alerting: paging if per-slice p99 > target*1.5 for 5m OR circuit-breaker rate > 0.5% of total requests for 3m. Links: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rel/latency-slice-overview
testing_plan: - Simulation harness: replay past month of traffic with injected region failures and capacity throttles. - Chaos: terminate region nodes in staging to validate failover behavior. - Load test: synthetic tails to ensure no regression in steady-state. - Integration: verify KV cache affinity preserved for pinned sessions. - Performance regression: microbench routing path latency must be <2ms median added.
open_risks: 1) Telemetry lag causing stale decisions — mitigation: conservative smoothing and fallback to capacity-preserving routing. 2) Oscillation during rapid autoscale — mitigation: tie scoring window to autoscaler smoothing and include explicit autoscale hints. 3) Egress cost during cross-region failover — mitigation: preferentially route to region-local cache and apply cost caps per customer tier.
integration_points: runtime: expose 'capacity_token_fraction' and 'prefetch_hit_rate' signals; console: add per-route SLO snapshot; dedicated: ensure reserved pools honor pinning and token accounting.
implementation_notes: Core components: (A) per-region metric collector (p50/p95/p99 rolling windows), (B) slice classifier (request metadata => latency slice), (C) router core scoring engine, (D) circuit-breaker and shedder module, (E) observability hooks. Persistent state: pinning table with TTL stored in Redis (sharded), scoring config in ConfigService with feature flags.
qa_and_validation: We will run end-to-end regression on staging with a CI job that replays historical incidents (see attachments). Gate: no VM/instance-level increased error budget during canary; manual approval required after phase 2.
next_steps: - PR for collector + scoring engine: opened. - Telemetry contract: finalize with Observability team. - Add tests in routing sim harness and schedule chaos run in staging.
